sections.content: Tucked between Seattle and Portland on the southern tip of Puget Sound, Olympia, WA doesn't always make the headlines in real estate investing circles. That's exactly what makes it interesting. While investors pile into Seattle's overheated market, Olympia quietly offers lower entry prices, steady population growth, and a government-backed economy that keeps vacancy rates low and demand consistent. Whether you're a wholesaler looking for your next assignment, a flipper hunting for distressed properties, or a landlord building a rental portfolio, there are real estate deals in Olympia WA worth paying attention to. If you're newer to the game, bookmark our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) guide first — it'll give you a strong foundation before you dive into a specific market.
Olympia WA Market Overview: Why Investors Are Taking Notice

Olympia is the state capital of Washington, home to roughly 55,000 residents within city limits and over 290,000 people across the greater Thurston County metro area. The local economy is anchored by state government jobs, Joint Base Lewis-McChord (about 20 miles north), healthcare, and a growing tech-adjacent workforce that commutes to the South Sound corridor. This combination creates something rare in real estate: a market that doesn't crash hard when the economy softens. Government workers still need housing, military families rotate in and out every few years, and the region's natural amenities — hiking, water access, outdoor recreation — keep attracting remote workers priced out of Seattle.

As of 2024, the median home price in Olympia sits around $415,000 to $440,000, depending on the data source and exact neighborhood. That's roughly half the Seattle metro median, which consistently tops $800,000. For investors, that lower price point means smaller capital requirements, easier financing, and faster paths to cash flow on rental properties. The average days on market hovers around 20 to 35 days for move-in-ready homes, while distressed or outdated properties can sit for 60 to 90 days — creating opportunities for patient investors who know what to look for. Explore the full breakdown of deal activity at our [Olympia WA market page](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/olympia-wa).
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Olympia

Not every zip code in Olympia performs the same way. Location still drives returns, and knowing which pockets offer the best opportunities can mean the difference between a deal that pays and one that drains your time and capital.
West Olympia and Westside Neighborhoods

West Olympia is the most desirable residential area in the city, featuring larger lots, mature trees, and homes built in the 1960s through 1990s. Median prices here run $480,000 to $550,000. For flippers, the play is finding outdated interiors — original kitchens, popcorn ceilings, dated bathrooms — in otherwise solid homes. A clean cosmetic flip in West Olympia can yield $60,000 to $90,000 in profit when executed well. Rentals here attract long-term, stable tenants including state workers and healthcare professionals.
Southeast Olympia and Lacey

Lacey, which borders Olympia to the east, is one of the fastest-growing cities in Washington state. It offers newer construction, strong retail infrastructure, and easy freeway access. For rental investors, Lacey delivers solid cap rates — typically 5% to 7% on single-family rentals when purchased right. Smaller duplexes and triplexes in the $500,000 to $650,000 range can cash flow $400 to $800 per month net after expenses, depending on financing terms. This is also a strong market for BRRRR strategy investors.
Downtown Olympia and the Eastside

Downtown Olympia and the Eastside neighborhoods offer the highest upside for wholesalers. Homes here are older — many built in the 1940s through 1970s — with more deferred maintenance, absentee owners, and inherited properties. Average prices in these areas run $320,000 to $380,000, well below the city median. Wholesale assignment fees of $15,000 to $30,000 are achievable on the right deals when you're connecting motivated sellers to active flippers and landlords in the area.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Olympia WA

items: Wholesale Deals: Distressed, inherited, or pre-foreclosure properties in East Olympia and downtown corridors. Assignment fees typically range from $10,000 to $35,000 depending on property condition and ARV.

Fix and Flip: Cosmetic flips in West Olympia and South Sound suburbs. Aim for a 70% ARV rule — use our free [ARV Calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/arv-calculator) to run comps before making any offer.
Buy and Hold Rentals: Single-family homes and small multifamily properties in Lacey and Tumwater offer reliable cash flow backed by military and government tenant pools.
BRRRR Strategy: Purchase distressed homes in Eastside Olympia, rehab, rent, refinance, and repeat. Refinance values have held steady thanks to consistent appreciation.
Short-Term Rentals: Proximity to the state capitol, outdoor recreation, and tourism creates demand for Airbnb-style rentals, particularly near the waterfront and Priest Point Park areas.

Olympia Real Estate Market Trends in 2024 and Beyond

Olympia's market has cooled slightly from the frenzied pace of 2021 and 2022, but it hasn't softened the way some West Coast markets have. Year-over-year price appreciation has settled into a more sustainable 3% to 5% range. Inventory remains constrained — new construction hasn't kept up with demand, particularly for workforce housing under $400,000. This supply gap is good news for both flippers (strong buyer demand for updated homes) and landlords (low vacancy rates, typically under 4% in Thurston County). Interest rates remain the biggest wildcard, but the spread between mortgage costs and rent rates in Olympia makes cash flow deals possible — especially when buyers bring 20-25% down or use creative financing structures.

"The best real estate markets aren't always the ones everyone is talking about. They're the ones with steady jobs, growing populations, and more sellers than buyers know what to do with." — Common wisdom among Pacific Northwest investors

One trend worth watching: Olympia is seeing increased interest from Seattle-based investors who've been squeezed out of King County. This outside capital is pushing prices up in the most desirable zip codes, but it's also creating more competition for flip-ready properties. To stay ahead, focus on off-market sourcing strategies. Check out our guide on [How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/off-market-real-estate-deals) for proven methods including direct mail, driving for dollars, and probate leads — all of which work well in Thurston County.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors Targeting Olympia

Olympia is a manageable market for remote investors, but you'll need a local team and a clear strategy before you commit capital from a distance. Here's what experienced out-of-state investors recommend:

items: Build Your Local Team First: Find a real estate agent experienced with investment properties, a local general contractor for rehab estimates, and a property manager if you plan to hold rentals. Olympia has a smaller investor community than Seattle, which means relationships go further here.

Use Data to Drive Decisions: Don't rely on gut feel when you can't walk the neighborhood. Learn how to analyze deals with data-driven tools. Our guide on [How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/how-to-analyze-real-estate-deals) walks through every metric that matters — from cap rate to cash-on-cash return.

Understand Washington State Landlord-Tenant Laws: Washington has strong tenant protections, including strict notice requirements and just-cause eviction rules in some municipalities. Know the rules before you buy a rental property.

Target Motivated Seller Lists: Pre-foreclosures, probate cases, tax-delinquent properties, and absentee owners are the four best lead sources in Olympia. Thurston County public records are accessible online and updated regularly.

Visit Before You Buy: Even one trip to walk neighborhoods and meet your contractor will save you from costly mistakes. What looks like a cosmetic flip in photos can reveal foundation issues or chronic moisture problems on a walkthrough.

Start with a Wholesale Deal: If you're new to the Olympia market, consider assigning your first deal rather than funding a flip yourself. You'll learn the market, build relationships, and generate revenue with minimal risk. Check out [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) if you need a primer on how the process works.

sections.content: Running the Numbers: A Quick Olympia Deal Example

Let's say you find a distressed single-family home in East Olympia listed off-market at $285,000. The property needs roughly $45,000 in rehab — new kitchen, updated bathrooms, fresh paint, and landscaping. Comparable sales in the neighborhood show ARVs of $415,000 to $430,000. Applying the 70% rule: $420,000 ARV x 70% = $294,000 minus $45,000 in rehab = a maximum purchase price of $249,000. At $285,000, this deal doesn't pencil for a flipper — but that gap is your negotiating room. Get the seller to $250,000 and you've got a potential $60,000 to $80,000 gross profit before holding costs and agent commissions. That's the math that makes Olympia worth pursuing.
